unit: one canonical pair of top-level inline comments from two different mapped reviewer products at the exact same original commit, path, and original diff position
selection_rule: Within each strict locus, order comments by valid creation timestamp and event id. Comment A is the earliest mapped-product comment; Comment B is the earliest comment at that locus from a different mapped product. Retain one pair per locus.

comment_A_substance.definition: Whether Comment A makes a code-review claim or request that can be compared with Comment B.

comment_B_substance.definition: Whether Comment B makes a code-review claim or request that can be compared with Comment A.

definitions.redundant_or_agreeing: The comments identify the same issue, request substantially the same change, or explicitly agree.
definitions.complementary: The comments address the same code locus but add materially different, compatible concerns or remedies.
definitions.contradictory: Following one comment would conflict with, undo, or directly reject the other comment's diagnosis or requested change.
definitions.unrelated_or_unclear: The visible text is insufficient, boilerplate, or concerns different topics whose relationship cannot be established.

confidence.definition: Coder confidence based only on the two comments and visible diff context.

evidence_note.definition: A short reason for the assigned relation; do not infer hidden intent or code correctness.

coding_rules: Code only the visible comment text and supplied diff context.
Do not infer that either reviewer is correct or that the code was changed.
Use unrelated_or_unclear when either comment cannot be interpreted well enough for a pairwise relation.
Product, repository, pull-request outcome, and raw identifiers remain hidden from coders.
language_policy: Labels describe visible semantic relations between public comments. They do not establish correctness, causal impact, repair, resolution, or private coordination.
